correctness.rationale: For \(n=3k+2\) every gamma-set has k+1 centers with exactly one short length-two cyclic gap, giving the n distinct rotations. The pair {0,2} realizes traces with multiplicities 1,k,k,k+1; every triple co-occurring in a gamma-set forces its third point whenever the two endpoints around the short gap are selected, excluding three-way shattering. The depth-three certificate uses 8 explicitly checked shift witnesses for all k>=3; the k+1-shift ordered-threshold subfamily yields floor(log2(k+1)) full adaptive levels. Entropy bounds Ldim above by floor(log2 n); for k=1 and k=2 the value 2 follows from VC lower and respectively cardinality or root-positive-branch count, and for k=3 the value 3 is exact. The extracted verifier independently enumerates all gamma-sets at k<=6 and recomputes exact Ldim; finite samples are not used to infer the infinite statement.

value.rationale: This determines the exact static dimension for a canonical infinite family of minimum-size domination systems and shows a logarithmically diverging adaptive/static shattering gap on connected vertex-transitive 2-regular graphs. The short-gap cyclic structure is a mathematically natural rigidity invariant; its exact implications for shattering are not a mere parameter relabeling. The two-sided logarithmic estimate has a constant-size additive uncertainty, and the first gap in this residue class is rigorously localized at n=11.
